justification: Takes the quarantined-test list from 16 files to ZERO, and installs a shrink-only ratchet in CI so it cannot silently refill. 3,970 -> 4,101 passing tests. Six files already passed; two were broken BY the quarantining itself; two had drifted behind the code and were repaired; five were not tests at all (1,090 lines, zero assertions) and were deleted; three needed a live server or a real database and now carry skip guards. Standard tier: it changes what the gates enforce for every future change, deletes files, and touches tests/conftest_mocks.py, which every one of the 4,101 tests imports.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: PROVEN by planting both enforcement rules and confirming each fires, with tests/conftest.py restored byte-identically afterwards (md5 8b180d569b8a0b28e7eabe4660acb8eb before and after both). RULE 1, no new debt: added test_flood_truth.py to collect_ignore with no baseline entry -> 'NEW quarantine, not in the baseline: test_flood_truth.py', exit 1. RULE 2, fixed means released: added test_upzoning_check.py to collect_ignore WITH a fabricated baseline entry -> 'BASELINE ENTRY NOW PASSES: test_upzoning_check.py -- now 13 passed', exit 1. RULE 3 also fired unplanned and caught a real mistake of mine: my plant-2 cleanup failed to revert the untracked baseline file, leaving a stale entry behind, and the check reported 'STALE BASELINE ENTRY ... Delete the entry.' The ratchet caught its own author within minutes of being written.
falsifiable_check.limits: The ratchet proves the quarantine list has not GROWN and that nothing in it has silently started passing. It says nothing about whether the ten remaining files SHOULD be fixed, and it cannot see a test that runs but asserts nothing. It reports that explicitly on every pass rather than printing an unqualified green.

pre_impl.existing_data: Measured before changing anything. All 16 quarantined files were run individually against the live database: 5 passed outright (35 tests), 1 was partial (50 pass / 27 fail), 10 were broken. Traced the origin with git log -S: every stale marker was added in ONE commit, 366f2054 on 2026-05-23, titled 'working test infrastructure + pre-push hook + CI' -- the commit that turned the gates on. Confirmed the exemption is invisible: the files sit in collect_ignore so pytest never collects them, they produce no skipped line, and `pytest -m stale` collects ZERO tests, meaning even a deliberate search finds nothing.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Assumed these tests were quarantined because they need infrastructure CI does not have (a running server, a live database) and therefore could not be turned on. WRONG for six of sixteen: they pass today with no changes at all. Worse, the assumption that quarantining is harmless was also wrong -- inserting 'import pytest / pytestmark = pytest.mark.stale' at the top of two files pushed 'from __future__ import annotations' below other statements, which is a SyntaxError. The quarantine did not merely hide broken tests, it CREATED two of them. test_lga_coverage.py has been un-runnable ever since for that reason alone.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: The shrink-only baseline pattern is copied deliberately from scripts/schema_contract_baseline.json rather than invented; its comment already states the two rules ('may only SHRINK... an entry that no longer occurs ALSO fails CI'). The CI step sits directly beside check_dependency_skips.py, its sibling for the other way a test stops running. No new pattern, no new dependency, no product code.

functions.name: quarantined_test_files
functions.input: no arguments; parses tests/conftest.py from disk
functions.output: sorted list of collect_ignore entries beginning with test_, read via ast rather than by importing conftest (importing would trigger its mock-injection side effects)
functions.if_none: returns an empty list when collect_ignore is absent or holds no test files, which the caller treats as zero debt rather than as an error

functions.name: run_one
functions.input: one test filename relative to tests/
functions.output: (passes_cleanly, summary). Runs pytest with -o addopts= so the ini's default deselection cannot hide the file from the check written to look at it
functions.if_none: a file that only skips, contains no tests, or errors on collection is NOT clean -- an all-skipped file protects nothing and promoting it would be the same self-deception one layer up

functions.name: load_baseline
functions.input: no arguments; reads and parses the JSON at tests/quarantine-baseline.json from disk
functions.output: dict keyed by filename, each carrying status, measured, error and cause
functions.if_none: a missing baseline file returns an empty dict, so every quarantined file then reports as new debt rather than being silently accepted

functions.name: pytest_report_header
functions.output: one line naming the number of quarantined files, printed at the top of every run
functions.if_none: returns None when nothing is quarantined, so the line disappears entirely once the debt reaches zero

values.value: 6 files released, 43 tests recovered (3,970 -> 4,013 before this PR's own new tests; 4,024 with them)
values.read_at: measured by running each quarantined file individually against the live database, 2026-08-09
values.why: The concrete answer to 'can we turn them on'. Five needed no changes whatsoever; the sixth needed only the import-order repair.
values.if_missing: Without measuring per file, the honest-sounding assumption -- 'they were quarantined for a reason, leave them' -- would have held, and 43 working tests would have stayed off indefinitely.

values.why: Changes the diagnosis completely. This is not gradual decay or neglect; it is the one-off cost of switching enforcement on, which nothing ever came back to pay down.
values.if_missing: Without the origin the fix would be framed as discipline ('remember to check'), which is exactly the kind of prose rule this project has already established does not hold.

values.why: Proves the exemption is invisible rather than merely quiet. The marker is dead weight; collect_ignore is what actually excludes them, and it reports nothing.
values.if_missing: The obvious fix would have been to lean on the marker, which does nothing at all here.

values.value: 2 files were broken BY the quarantining
values.read_at: SyntaxError on 'from __future__ import annotations'; confirmed by restoring the legal import order and re-running -- test_lga_coverage.py then collected 12 tests
values.why: The quarantine did not just conceal broken tests, it manufactured two. That is a much stronger argument for a visible list than mere untidiness.
values.if_missing: These two would have been recorded as legitimately broken and left alone, when the repair was a two-line reordering.

break_it.scenario: The baseline becomes the new hiding place — entries are added and never removed, exactly as collect_ignore was.
break_it.what_happens: The same failure with more ceremony: a longer list, still unread, still permanent. This is the single most likely way this PR fails to achieve anything.
break_it.how: Rule 2 is the answer and is why this is a ratchet rather than a baseline. A listed file that starts passing FAILS CI, so fixing a test forces its removal from the list. A baseline that only guards against growth would allow permanent amnesty; this one makes entries decay. Proven by planting a passing file with a fabricated entry.
break_it.repro: Add a known-good file (e.g. test_upzoning_check.py) to collect_ignore with a baseline entry, then run scripts/check_test_quarantine.py -- expect 'BASELINE ENTRY NOW PASSES' and exit 1.

break_it.scenario: A file is quietly added to collect_ignore when it starts failing, instead of being fixed.
break_it.what_happens: Debt grows invisibly, which is precisely the 15-month pattern this replaces.
break_it.how: Rule 1: any collect_ignore entry beginning with test_ that has no baseline entry fails CI with a message naming the file. Proven by planting test_flood_truth.py.
break_it.repro: Add any test file to collect_ignore without a baseline entry and run the checker -- expect 'NEW quarantine, not in the baseline' and exit 1.

break_it.scenario: A released file was only ever passing because every one of its tests skips, so releasing it adds coverage that does not exist.
break_it.what_happens: The test count rises and protects nothing — a flattering number, which is the failure mode this whole line of work exists to stop.
break_it.how: run_one treats an all-skipped file as NOT clean, so the ratchet will not demand its release and it stays quarantined until it genuinely runs. test_lga_coverage.py is exactly this case: it now collects 12 tests but every one skips, so it remains in the baseline with that recorded as its status rather than being counted as a win.

break_it.scenario: The stale marker deselects a quarantined file from the very check meant to inspect it, so the ratchet reports 'no tests ran' regardless of the file's real state.
break_it.what_happens: The checker would report every quarantined file as still broken forever, including ones that had been fixed — silently defeating rule 2 while appearing to work.
break_it.how: run_one passes -o addopts= to clear the ini's -m "not stale and not database" default. Pinned by a test that builds a pytest.ini with a deselecting addopts and a marked test file, and asserts the result is still seen.

break_it.scenario: Releasing six files destabilises the suite — a released test is flaky, or depends on the live database, and main goes red intermittently.
break_it.what_happens: Red main, and the likeliest response is to re-quarantine, undoing the PR and reinforcing the original habit.
break_it.how: Partially, and the residual is stated. All six were run individually AND in the full suite: 4,024 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed. Four of the six carry their own DATABASE_URL guards and skip cleanly without it, which is why the CI environment does not need to change. NOT established: behaviour over time. If one proves flaky, the correct response is to fix or re-quarantine it WITH a baseline entry recording why — which the ratchet now forces, so even a regression leaves evidence.
break_it.repro: python -m pytest -q with and without DATABASE_URL set; both must be green.

break_it.scenario: A malformed baseline file makes the gate error out instead of reporting, so a broken checker reads as an infrastructure problem rather than as unrecorded debt.
break_it.what_happens: load_baseline used .get('entries', []); with "entries": null present, the default does not apply and iteration raises. CI would show a crashed step, which gets triaged as flaky tooling and skipped, and the quarantine list stops being checked at all — the original failure, restored.
break_it.how: Uses (data.get('entries') or []) so a null or malformed entries block degrades to an empty baseline. That makes every quarantined file report as NEW debt and fails loudly, which is the correct direction for a gate: a broken baseline must not fail open. Caught by the qa_gate Python-adversarial check, not by me.
break_it.repro: Set "entries": null in tests/quarantine-baseline.json and run scripts/check_test_quarantine.py -- it must report every quarantined file as new debt and exit 1, not raise TypeError.

break_it.scenario: The lazy RAGProcessor import hides a genuinely missing dependency until deep inside a run, or breaks a caller that relied on eager import.
break_it.what_happens: Someone calling RAGProcessor in one of the two scripts that use it would hit the failure later than before, or `from src.processing import RAGProcessor` would stop working.
break_it.how: PEP 562 module __getattr__ keeps `from src.processing import RAGProcessor` working -- the name resolves on access and the ORIGINAL ImportError propagates, so the message still names `raganything` rather than a vague AttributeError. Deliberately NOT set to None on failure, which would have produced 'NoneType is not callable' far from the cause. Checked first: RAGProcessor appears in no file under services/, i.e. no deployed code path; only two one-off scripts use it.
break_it.repro: python -c "from src.processing import SchemaExtractor" must succeed without raganything; python -c "import src.processing as p; p.RAGProcessor" must raise ImportError naming raganything.

break_it.scenario: The PYTEST_REAL_DB opt-in changes behaviour for the 4,101 tests that do not ask for it.
break_it.what_happens: If the psycopg2 stub were skipped automatically whenever the real library is installed, thousands of pure-logic tests would start attempting real connections on any dev machine — silent, widespread, and hard to attribute.
break_it.how: Opt-IN via an explicit environment variable, never automatic. Default runs are byte-for-byte unchanged: measured 4,101 passed before and after the conftest_mocks edit. One real bug surfaced while building it — the RealDictCursor patch did an unguarded sys.modules lookup that raised KeyError and killed the ENTIRE run at conftest load under the new flag; it is now guarded, and only the stub is ever patched, never the genuine library.
break_it.repro: python -m pytest -q (expect 4,101 passed) then PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 DATABASE_URL=... python -m pytest tests/test_lga_coverage.py -o addopts= (expect it to connect and run, not skip).

break_it.scenario: Releasing conditionally-runnable tests inflates the skip count, and the dependency-skip ratchet — the sibling gate — refuses the change.
break_it.what_happens: Exactly what happened: skips went 2 -> 16 and CI failed with 'SKIP-TOTAL RATCHET: FAILED — 16 skipped test(s) against a baseline of 2'. The tempting fix is to raise that baseline, which would blunt a working gate to accommodate my change and make future genuine skip growth invisible.
break_it.how: Baseline NOT raised. The tests are DESELECTED instead, via a new `integration` marker in pytest.ini's addopts alongside the existing `database` one, and test_lga_coverage.py re-marked `database`. A test that needs a server this environment does not have is not a skipped test, it is a test for a different environment — so it should not consume the skip budget. Result: back to 2 skipped, 75 deselected, and both markers still reachable (`pytest -m integration` shows 14, `-m database` collects 31).
break_it.repro: python scripts/check_dependency_skips.py must report against baseline without failing; python -m pytest -q must show 2 skipped, not 16.

mutation_analysis: Both enforcement rules were planted and each fired with a specific message; conftest.py restored byte-identically (md5 identical). A third rule fired unplanned against a genuine error of my own -- a failed cleanup left a stale baseline entry and the checker demanded its deletion. The ratchet's own 11 tests were written to cover the cases most likely to be quietly weakened later: the all-skip case, the no-tests case, and the marker-hiding case. Weak assertions avoided: the tests assert on the clean/not-clean decision and the summary text rather than on exit codes alone, because an exit code cannot distinguish 'no tests ran' from 'all skipped', and those two need different responses.
residual_risk: The list is empty, which is NOT the same as the tests being good. Three specific limits. (1) test_lga_coverage.py now runs, and on its first real execution FAILED on a genuine defect: Marrickville has 14.8% NULL v2_topic (583 of 3,934) against a 10% threshold. That is an open data-quality finding this PR surfaces and does not fix. (2) That gate still only checks 4 hardcoded councils, in a slug format that does not match production, and does NOT read the enabled-councils list — so it cannot notice a council being switched on. Rewriting it was attempted and deliberately STOPPED: the check is tier-dependent and no machine-readable tier map exists. Tier 2 councils promise numeric controls ONLY, so having no provision text is their DESIGNED state, not a defect; a naive derived gate would fail 13 councils that are working as intended. That is a product decision. (3) 16 tests now report as skips (live server or database absent). Visible and actionable, but not coverage. Unchanged elsewhere: the liability scanner still reads only changed lines, CI still runs no frontend build.

post_merge.db_reset: None. No migration, no schema change, no database write. Tests were run against the live database read-only to establish which files pass; nothing was written.
post_merge.secrets: None added or read. Four of the released files skip cleanly when DATABASE_URL is absent, which is how CI already runs them.
post_merge.other_repo: None. No sibling repository or deployment target affected.
post_merge.manual_verify: Confirm the first line of CI's pytest output reads 'quarantined: 10 test files excluded from collection', and that the 'Quarantined tests (shrink-only ratchet)' step appears and passes. Then confirm the count in .claude/rules/testing-and-qa.md still matches reality -- it is the number that will drift first, and it now has a command beside it to re-derive.
